content.thinking:
I need to fix a bug where background work on workspaces has become unreliable as the number of workspaces grew.

The issue affects overdue alerts, daily digests, and retention cleanup. Some workspaces are skipped entirely on each run. Members with unread notifications receive nothing. Expired archived content is also left untouched for weeks.

The periodic usage recount repeatedly corrects the same workspaces while leaving others with drifting counters. Deleted workspaces still trigger overdue alerts. Every run must cover all non-deleted workspaces.

Each covered workspace must still behave exactly as it does today. Deleted workspaces receive no alerts or digests. The usage recount is intentionally incremental: each run processes at most 25 workspaces and selects the oldest counters, moving them to the back of the queue.

content.text: I'll look through the background jobs that scan workspaces and find why some are skipped or repeated.

content.thinking: The bug is that all these jobs use `usageRepo`.
Overdue, digest, and cleanup all call `listOrgIdsForRollup`, which returns only a limited batch of orgs ordered by most recently measured first. This is the root cause.

Deleted organizations are archived rather than permanently removed.

The overdue job currently includes archived organizations. It should only cover active workspaces. Deleted workspaces must receive no alerts or digests. Usage recounting needs a separate `recountedAt` timestamp so `incrementUsage` cannot shift a workspace in the queue.

`listOrgIdsForRollup` orders workspaces by `recountedAt` ascending, oldest first, and limits to 25. Other jobs must list all non-archived organizations.

Retention cleanup is capped at 25 organizations and 100 archived issues per run. This leaves some workspaces untouched for weeks. Pagination within archived issues may also be a problem if more than 100 exist.

Per-workspace logic must remain unchanged. The overdue job should list all non-archived organizations, while the digest job already excludes archived workspaces via its `archivedAt` check.

Retention cleanup must also exclude deleted workspaces. The overdue, digest, and cleanup jobs will each use the full list of non-archived organizations instead of `listOrgIdsForRollup`. A `recountedAt` column on `organization_usage` needs to be added.

The queue ordering by `measuredAt` descending is the root cause. `recomputeUsage` and `incrementUsage` both update that timestamp to the current time, so active workspaces never leave the front of the list. This explains why the same workspaces are repeatedly recounted while others are ignored.

content.thinking:
I need to check how migrate applies ALTER for existing databases.

A separate `recountedAt` column is needed so `incrementUsage` can update queue position without touching `measuredAt`. Otherwise the queue would shift to the back on every usage bump.

`measuredAt` should remain the public "last measured" timestamp for billing display. `recountedAt` will be used solely for queue ordering, set only by `recomputeUsage`. `incrementUsage` and `getUsage` inserts will leave it null so workspaces stay at the front of the queue.

The queue will order by `recounted_at ASC NULLS FIRST`, with `org_id` as a tie-breaker. Organizations without usage rows are skipped because the rollup job only processes existing records.

The queue currently sorts by `measuredAt DESC`, which traps older workspaces at the back and causes them to be recounted repeatedly while newer ones drift away. I should left-join organizations with usage so every workspace is included, not just those with existing rows. I also need to decide whether deleted workspaces should be counted.

Deleted workspaces will remain in the recount queue. The bug fix only changes ordering and timestamps, so eligibility is unchanged. Cleanup already excludes deleted workspaces.

A new `listActiveOrgIds` query will return every active organization without a limit. Digest, overdue, and cleanup will all iterate over the full set.

Cleanup currently caps at 25 workspaces and only fetches the first page of issues. The bug requires covering all workspaces, so I will not change the page size unless necessary.

The "leaves some workspaces untouched for weeks" issue is workspace-level, not issue-level. The existing page size is likely intentional.

/**
 * Brings `databasePath` up to date. Generated migrations win when they exist;
 * otherwise the embedded schema is pushed. Safe to run repeatedly — every
 * statement is `IF NOT EXISTS`.
 */
export async function runMigrations(
  databasePath: string = process.env.TASKFLOW_DB_PATH ?? DEFAULT_DB_PATH,
): Promise<void> {
  const absolute = resolve(process.cwd(), databasePath);
  mkdirSync(dirname(absolute), { recursive: true });

  const sqlite = new Database(absolute);
  sqlite.pragma("journal_mode = WAL");

  try {
    for (const statement of readMigrationStatements()) {
      sqlite.exec(statement);
    }
  } finally {
    sqlite.close();
  }
}
